channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Oil: Strait of Hormuz risks reshape macro mix – BNY
item.description: BNY's Geoff Yu notes that renewed U.S.-Iran tensions have lifted Brent and WTI, with markets reassessing energy supply risks and broader risk sentiment.

item.title: Euro climbs above 1.1400 as US Dollar loses ground
item.description: EUR/USD trades with a mild positive bias on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) gives back its earlier gains. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1424 after recovering from an intraday low of 1.1384.

item.title: US President Trump: We are taking over the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: In an interview with Fox News on Monday, United States (US) President Donald Trump said that they will probably take over the Strait of Hormuz and argued that they should be reimbursed for controlling it.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Range holds as markets await Warsh and CPI – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes that the US Dollar Index (DXY) Index has been confined between 100.5 and 102 for three weeks as traders await clarity on whether the Federal Reserve (Fed) will proceed with a potential rate hike later this year.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Consolidation near resistance band against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux describes USD/JPY consolidating after failing again at resistance near 162.80. The pair is seen in a narrow range, with key support at 160.40 tied to the March peak and upside projections towards 163.70/164.40 if resistance breaks.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ tightening risks watched – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Lee Sue Ann and Jester Koh note that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand raised the Official Cash Rate to 2.50% in July and adopted a more hawkish tone as inflation risks remain elevated.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD drifts below $4,100, but bears start to look exhausted
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends losses on Monday, with price action drifting below the $4,100 line, amid a risk-off market mood, as tensions between the US and Iran flare.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Supported against US Dollar by steady BoC outlook – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that the Bank of Canada (BoC) is widely expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 2.25%, with markets not pricing cuts until at least Q4.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Bounces back to near 1.3400 as US Dollar turns upside down
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) recovers its early losses and flattens around 1.3400 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed data focus supports modest gains – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) traded mixed, but expects USD to edge slightly higher over the next couple of months as US labor markets stabilize and inflation remains sticky.

item.title: Kiwi nears 0.5800 as RBNZ tightening hopes offset risk aversion
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) retraced previous losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday and trades higher for the fourth consecutive day, approaching three-week highs near 0.5800.

item.title: Gold declines as renewed US-Iran hostilities boost Oil prices, Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) starts the week on the back foot as renewed tensions in the Middle East lift Oil prices and bring inflation concerns back into focus, reinforcing expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike later this year.

item.title: Swiss Franc: ECB support limits gains against euro – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/CHF performance since the Iran war, noting that the Swiss National Bank (SNB) has intervened to counter safe haven inflows while the European Central Bank’s (ECB) hawkish stance has supported the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish NBP pressures PLN against Euro – ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky says Central and Eastern European FX will be driven by secondary data and policy expectations. A dovish National Bank of Poland stance and market pricing of future rate cuts are seen weighing on the Zloty, with ING’s models pointing EUR/PLN closer to 4.340.

item.title: Indian Rupee weakens amid surging Oil prices, India's CPI rises strongly
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades significantly lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday. The USD/INR jumps to over a six-week high around 95.70 as renewed Middle East hostilities have strengthened oil prices.

item.title: India’s retail CPI rises strongly by 4.38% in June, beats 4.3% estimates
item.description: India’s retail Consumer Price Index (CPI) rises at an annualized pace of 4.38% in June, stronger than 4.3% estimates and the previous reading of 3.93%.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Momentum fades into sideways band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann observe that AUD/USD has been range‑trading slightly higher than expected, with intraday levels seen between 0.6920 and 0.6960. The earlier tentative upside momentum has faded, and for the next 1–3 weeks the pair is expected to trade between 0.6890 and 0.6975.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Range-bound trade risks around CPI – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that India’s June Consumer Price Index (CPI) release will be important for bond markets, with the 10-year IGB yield holding near its 200-day moving average around 6.71%.

item.title: British Pound: Gilt confidence and new leadership – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that United Kingdom (UK) assets, including the British Pound (GBP) and gilts, will react more to the choice of chancellor under incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham than to the leadership change itself.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Wavers around 0.6950 with bearish momentum fading
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) posts marginal losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as the pair's reversal from Friday's 0.6970 highs found support above 0.6120. Rising tensions in Iran have hammered risk appetite, but the US Dollar’s weakness is keeping the Aussie from retreating further.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.72 per troy ounce, down 1.92% from the $59.87 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Oil: Markets price renewed Hormuz risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Michael Every discusses rising geopolitical risks around the Strait of Hormuz after the apparent collapse of a US-Iran memorandum of understanding. Every notes both sides are now striking each other, with United States (US) strategy shifting to escorted energy flows.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher energy supports Fed tightening – ING
item.description: ING analysts Chris Turner, Frantisek Taborsky and Francesco Pesole note that higher energy prices and tensions in the Gulf are supporting the Dollar against low-yielding currencies. They highlight that US energy independence and live Fed tightening prospects underpin Dollar strength.

item.title: Euro recovers early losses against Canadian Dollar, BoC policy eyed
item.description: The Euro (EUR) claws back its early losses and turns slightly positive at around 1.6170 against the Canadian Dollar (CAD) during the European trading session on Monday. The cross bounces back as the Euro strengthens amid hopes that the ongoing aggression in the Middle East won’t be prolonged.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Rises to near 1.1450 after breaking above nine-day EMA
item.description: EUR/USD gains ground after posting losses in the previous day, trading around 1.1440 during the European hours on Monday. The currency pair holds just above the nine-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) but remains capped by the 50-day EMA, keeping the near-term tone cautiously bearish.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Mixed outlook within defined band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that USD/JPY rebounded after a sharp drop to 161.26, with intraday gains expected to be capped between 161.60 and 162.45. Over the next 1–3 weeks, the outlook is described as mixed, with trading likely between 160.60 and 163.00.

item.title: United States Dollar Index Price Forecast: Bears await break below 23.6% Fibo. near 100.80
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, attracts some sellers following an intraday uptick to the 101.22 area on Monday and fills a modest weekly bullish gap.

item.title: Iran confirms Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan continue to mediate with US
item.description: A spokesperson from the Iranian Foreign Ministry has confirmed in the European trade on Monday that efforts from Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan to mediate tensions with the United States (US) continue.

item.title: Brent: Rebound tests key resistance – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux notes that Brent has sharply rebounded after defending the late-February low around $69 and is now testing the 200-day moving average and a descending trendline.

item.title: Gold pares intraday losses; keeps the red below $4,100 amid hawkish Fed expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trims a part of its intraday losses during the first half of the European session on Monday, though it retains the negative bias for the second straight day and remains below the $4,100 mark. The US Dollar (USD) attracts some intraday sellers and supports the bullion.
